subject: RPS vs tokens/sec: acceptance pathway & measurement plan for Dedicated commit
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Anna Lee <anna.lee@dataverse.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 22 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: RPS vs tokens/sec: acceptance pathway & measurement plan for Dedicated commit

Hi Anna —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Per our discussion, I wanted to put a short, pragmatic acceptance pathway in writing so we can align commercial terms (reserved commit + discount band) to measurable outcomes. High level ask from DataVerse: predictable token throughput for batch embedding and chat-generation workloads plus a 95th percentile latency target for interactive flows.

Proposal (summary):
- Commit: 48 GPU-months (8 GPUs steady) with 6-month ramp.
- Commercial ask: tiered discount tied to measured tokens/sec and request/sec bands (see attached spreadsheet for pricing bands).
- Acceptance: Redwood will run a joint verification run using your representative trace + our benchmark harness. Passing criteria are a contract-level guarantee for:
  * sustained aggregate tokens/sec across the pool (measured over 15m windows): target 2.5M tokens/sec sustained for batch peak, and
  * interactive SLO: p95 generation latency <= 350ms for 4k-context chat (model: open-llama-70b-q4v3 or agreed equivalent), measured under production-like concurrency (concurrency pattern supplied by DataVerse), and
  * availability during test: >= 99.5% for API success responses (excludes planned warm-up and infra maintenance).

Measurement methodology (brief):
1) Test inputs: 3 datasets — (a) representative prod trace you provided (sampled to 1:10), (b) synthetic wide-length mix for worst-case (10-8k tokens), (c) typical batch embedding payloads (avg 512 tokens).
2) Warm-up: 20-minute warm-up per node to populate KV cache and JIT paths; warm-up traffic excluded from measurement windows.
3) Windows: run three full 15-minute measurement windows after warm-up; the median window must meet aggregate tokens/sec and latency p95 targets.
4) Measurement points: tokens/sec (aggregate and per-GPU), requests/sec (aggregate), p50/p95/p99 latency, error rate, CPU/GPU utilization, and KV cache hit rate.
5) Environment: Redwood-managed cluster (same instance types reserved in the commit) with network emulation to approximate your region latency. Test harness will be run by Redwood with optional read-only access for your SRE.

Failure & credits:
- If the median window misses the tokens/sec band by <=10% but latency target is met, we propose a 10% invoice credit for the first month post-commit activation to cover the ramp adjustment.
- Miss >10% or latency misses => joint remediation plan and escalating credits per SLA schedule in the attached pricing bands.

Next steps:
- If you like this framing I can attach the benchmark script and suggested CLI to run a mirrored test from your side, and we can book a 2-hour joint run next week.

Attaching: dv-throughput-spec-v2.xlsx (pricing bands), redwood-benchmark-script.sh (harness).

Thanks,
Karthik
Senior Sales Engineer
Redwood Inference
From: Anna Lee <anna.lee@dataverse.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: DataVerse SRE Team <sre@dataverse.com>
Date: Tue, 22 Sep 2026 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: RPS vs tokens/sec: acceptance pathway & measurement plan for Dedicated commit

Karthik —

Thanks for the clear summary. A few clarifying questions before we lock calendared runs: 
1) Tokens/sec definition: are you measuring raw model tokens emitted by the model, or input+output tokens? Which tokeniser are you using for the measurement?
2) For batch embedding runs (512 tokens avg), do you treat them as token throughput or as embedding-ops/sec for billing tiers? We need an apples-to-apples metric for our capacity planning team.
3) The warm-up approach is reasonable — can we shorten the node warm-up to 10 minutes if we run a previous warm cache snapshot?

On the latency side: p95 <=350ms for 4k-context is aggressive but aligns with our product goal. We need to confirm the model variant and quantization level used — we prefer not to accept a q4v1 path for the p95 target. Can you explicitly list the model binary (name + quant) you intend to use for the acceptance run?

Finally, regarding credits: curious if there's a one-time engineering goodwill credit if the acceptance run shows minor infra variance, since we have internal launch deadlines.

Thanks,
Anna
Head of Platform
DataVerse Inc.
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Anna Lee <anna.lee@dataverse.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 23 Sep 2026 11:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: RPS vs tokens/sec: acceptance pathway & measurement plan for Dedicated commit

Anna —

Quick answers inline, plus some operational clarifications so the acceptance run is unambiguous.

On Tue, Sep 22, 2026 at 10:03 AM Anna Lee <anna.lee@dataverse.com> wrote:
> 1) Tokens/sec definition: are you measuring raw model tokens emitted by the model, or input+output tokens? Which tokeniser are you using for the measurement?

We measure emitted model tokens (output tokens) and report input tokens separately. For fairness we use the byte-pair tokenizer matching the model family (we'll run with the open-llama tokenizer for the acceptance run). The primary billing/commercial metric will be output tokens/sec for generation-heavy flows; embeddings measured as embedding-ops (per request) and normalized into token-equivalent in the pricing bands in the spreadsheet.

> 2) For batch embedding runs (512 tokens avg), do you treat them as token throughput or as embedding-ops/sec for billing tiers?

We will report both. For contract bands we convert embedding-ops into a token-equivalent using the conversion table in dv-throughput-spec-v2.xlsx (row 12). That keeps the commit math consistent.

> 3) The warm-up approach is reasonable — can we shorten the node warm-up to 10 minutes if we run a previous warm cache snapshot?

Yes. If you supply a cache snapshot (read-only) and it's verified, we can do a 10-minute warm-up. We'll note this in the test-run plan and include the snapshot checksum in the run report.

> model variant and quantization

For the acceptance run we propose open-llama-70b-q4v3 as the primary candidate. If you require a different quant path, we can run parallel validation on q4v2/q8 models but the latency bands will differ. We'll include the exact binary sha in the final run report.

Engineering credit question:
We can offer a one-time goodwill credit equal to 5% of the first invoice month if the acceptance run misses by <=8% and there is evidence of non-deterministic infra variance (network flapping, transient OOMs) that was outside normal capacity behavior. This is additive to the ramp credits I proposed earlier.

Operational notes: reportable metrics will be exported as a CSV + Grafana snapshot. We'll provide read-only access to the Grafana dashboard after the run.

If this looks good I'll have Aditya coordinate schedules with your SRE and propose two 2-hour slots for next Tue/Wed.

—Marissa
Director, Customer Success
Redwood Inference

Marissa / Karthik —

That all sounds reasonable and fair. We accept open-llama-70b-q4v3 for the primary acceptance run and will provide a cache snapshot export (sha256: 9f3b2a...) ahead of time. Please book the joint run for Tue 2026-09-29 10:00-12:00 PT; SRE will attend and will validate metrics live.

Please also add the agreed 5% goodwill credit clause in the SOW appendix so legal has a clear reference.

Thanks,
